headline: Semis Lead a Broad Tuesday Rally as Geopolitical Winds Shift
body_html:
Tuesday's session delivered a convincing advance across nearly every corner of the market, with 434 of the 549 names in our universe closing higher against just 114 decliners. The dominant theme was risk appetite rekindled by signs of diplomatic movement in the Middle East: reports that a Strait of Hormuz agreement could materialize within days sent oil prices sharply lower, easing one of the market's most persistent cost-of-capital anxieties and freeing capital to rotate into equities broadly.

Semiconductors led all sectors with a gain of 7.11%, a commanding margin over Materials (+2.55%), Industrials (+2.43%), and Software (+2.12%). Arm Holdings surged 17.36%, supplying much of the sector's upward momentum. The session's standout mover, however, was Zebra Technologies, which vaulted 26.47% in the Tech-Hardware space after what appeared to be a strong earnings catalyst, edging out UFP Technologies (+25.16%) and Inspire Medical Systems (+22.81%) for the day's top honors.

The session's lone notable soft spot was in pockets of Healthcare infrastructure and specialty manufacturing. Bruker shed 21.79% in a punishing reversal for life-science tools, while Sterling Infrastructure and Rockwell Automation each gave back more than seven points. Breadth this decisive — nearly four advancers for every decliner — suggests Tuesday's move carried genuine conviction rather than a narrow, index-driven drift.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Optimism Drags Crude, Lifts Equities
briefs.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent's suggestion that a Strait of Hormuz arrangement could be formalized within the week sent oil prices tumbling, removing a meaningful inflation premium from the market's calculus. Equities responded immediately, with risk assets rallying across the board as the geopolitical discount began to unwind.

briefs.headline: Bruker Suffers Session's Sharpest Decline
briefs.body: Life-science tools maker Bruker closed down 21.79%, the steepest loss in our universe on Tuesday. The move appeared tied to company-specific earnings or guidance concerns rather than any broad sector retreat, as other Healthcare sub-groups managed modest positive returns on the day.

briefs.headline: Gartner Jumps on Research Demand Signal
briefs.body: Research-subscription firm Gartner surged 22.62%, placing it among the session's elite advancers. The move suggests institutional investors are rewarding companies with recurring, contract-based revenue streams — a preference consistent with a market still mindful of macro uncertainty even as sentiment brightens.

briefs.headline: US-Iran Diplomatic Channel Opens Further
briefs.body: Qatar confirmed meaningful progress toward US-Iran discussions aimed at ending the ongoing conflict, while separate State Department comments indicated Israel-Lebanon talks have formally commenced. The compounding diplomatic activity across the region appears to have been a significant catalyst for Tuesday's broad market advance.

briefs.headline: Tidewater Catches a Wave in Offshore Energy
briefs.body: Offshore-vessel operator Tidewater surged 17.77% even as broader crude prices fell, suggesting investors are differentiating between oil-price exposure and energy-services demand. The stock's move may reflect expectations that ongoing regional instability will sustain elevated activity levels for marine logistics operators regardless of near-term commodity swings.

briefs.headline: Manufacturing Data Adds Economic Confidence
briefs.body: Fresh data signaling a rebound in domestic manufacturing activity provided additional fundamental footing beneath Tuesday's rally. The figures complement the session's risk-on tone, reinforcing the view that the broader industrial economy is holding up despite protracted geopolitical headwinds, and lending support to the Industrials sector's 2.43% gain.
